relevance_note: The paper reports three children with heterozygous TNFAIP3 mutations: "Genetic testing showed that all three patients had heterozygous mutation in TNFAIP3 gene."
method_note: Read the paper fully; JSON built with a short Python script whose values were all typed from my reading; spans checked verbatim by script. Table 1 has patients as columns (headers Patient1, Patient2, Patient3); Table 2 has patients as rows. Table 1 uses '+' and '–' with no legend; '+' read as present, '–' left not reported (symbol not defined as absent). Table 2 '–' and 'N' cells left not reported. Labels: the paper uses 'Patient 1/2' and 'patient 3', heading 'Case 3' and Table 1 'Patient3'; 'Patient 3' chosen. Variant-to-patient assignment comes from each case narrative (P1 c.925-927dup, P2 c.1906 + 1G > C, P3 c.547C > T); the Results list gives the three variants in a different order than the patients. Inheritance for P1 and P2 left not reported: the paper calls c.1906 + 1G > C and c.925_927dup 'spontaneous mutations' after Sanger sequencing and says parental blood was collected, but never states the variant was absent in both parents. Parents of P1 and P2 are included only because figure captions show maps of gene mutations of each patient's father and mother (tested relatives); no results stated for them. Father of P3 tested negative. Mother of P3 carries the variant (zygosity not stated). Two previously published individuals from the Discussion's literature summary ('One case presented with...') are included as unnamed person 1 and 2; no reference is given for them. Other '1 case of X' items in that summary were treated as counts and given no rows. Ages at admission recorded as age at last evaluation; follow-up continued afterwards (3-4 months). Onset ages are given only relative to admission, so onset age is not reported. Time-bound absences at onset that were later contradicted were not recorded as excluded (P1 'no fever' and 'no bloody stool' at onset; P3 'no abdominal pain' at onset, later intermittent abdominal pain). Normal ANA/ANCA panels were recorded as excluded features but did not exclude the broader checklist item 'autoantibodies (ANA/other)'. 'No eye discomfort' and 'no rash' did not exclude the composite ocular and skin checklist items. Enhanced CT of thorax and abdomen negative was not used to exclude anything specific. Contradictions/inconsistencies: P1 is called 'girl' and 'her' but also 'a 91 cm and 11.5 kg boy' (female recorded; Methods says 1 male, 2 female and P3 is the boy). P2 height '105 cm' on examination vs 'only 130 cm at age 11'. P2 Table 1 'Renal damage +' while urine tests and 24-h urinary protein were normal and renal biopsy not performed. P2 ANA 1:100 and 1:1000 in text vs 'ANA 1:320' in Table 2. P3 CRP 105 mg/L in text vs 17.5 in Table 2. Discussion says steroids were not used in two of three patients, yet P2 received oral methylprednisolone and P3 steroids. Follow-up duration for P1 stated as four months (abstract) and 3 months on adalimumab. Figure numbering inconsistent: text says Fig. 4 shows P2 and Fig. 5 shows P3 gene maps, but captions label Fig. 3 as Patient 2 and Fig. 4 as Patient 3, and Fig. 5 is CT/MRI.
